title: Walking Cat
body:
Goal: use a forever loop and costumes to make the cat walk back and forth. Tool: Scratch app (offline). Work in pairs: swap driver and navigator when the timer rings.

Build steps

  1. Start a new project: File > New.
  2. Click the Costumes tab (top left). The cat has 2 costumes. Switching between them looks like walking. Click the Code tab to go back.
  3. Build the script below. set rotation style and if on edge, bounce are in Motion; forever and wait are in Control; next costume is in Looks.
  4. Click the green flag. Click the red stop sign to stop.
  5. Experiment: take out the wait block. What changes? Put it back.
  6. Save as walking-cat.

The script in words

Cat sprite:

  • when green flag clicked
  • set rotation style left-right
  • forever:
    • move 10 steps
    • next costume
    • if on edge, bounce
    • wait 0.1 seconds

Expected behavior

After the green flag, the cat walks across the stage, moving its legs. At the edge it turns round (and stays the right way up) and walks back. It keeps going until you click the red stop sign. Without the wait, the cat zooms and its legs flicker too fast to see.

Checklist

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Look for the loop that never stops. It is in the Control category. Everything the cat does again and again goes inside this loop.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Use a forever block from Control. Inside it, put one block that moves the cat and one that changes the costume. Add if on edge, bounce from Motion so the cat turns around, and a short wait from Control.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Before the loop, add set rotation style ( ) from Motion, and pick left-right so the cat never turns upside down. Inside forever, put the blocks that move, change the costume (Looks), bounce at the edge, and wait. Keep the wait small.
